compute_signals.subproblem: Exhaustive in-silico enumeration of capsid-receptor binding signatures (structure prediction + docking + free-energy refinement) across AAV variant libraries x AAVR/glycan/LY6A/LY6C1/CA4/ALPL/LRP6 ectodomains
compute_signals.what_compute_buys: Coverage of 10^5-10^6 capsid-receptor pairs that no wet-lab assay can match, revealing whether a compact, transferable binding-signature class exists at all or whether the map is irreducibly sparse and high-dimensional.

compute_signals.subproblem: Physics-based simulation of the post-binding sorting decision (endosomal pH-dependent dissociation, receptor clustering/geometry, ubiquitination, vesicle fate: recycling vs transcytosis vs lysosome) on brain microvascular endothelial cells
compute_signals.what_compute_buys: An in-silico sufficiency test of whether binding energetics plus trafficking kinetics jointly determine transcytosis versus retention, which would rank the handful of perturbations (receptor KO, GPI-anchor disruption, Rab17/Mfsd2a manipulation) that actually discriminate sufficiency from insufficiency.

compute_signals.subproblem: Hierarchical cross-species model fitting on pooled barcoded/TRACER/CREATE/transwell capsid datasets, with species, strain, and model-system (iBMEC vs primary BMEC) random effects
compute_signals.what_compute_buys: Quantifies the explained variance attributable to binding signatures alone and whether any signature transfers from mouse strains to NHP/human or is species-locked, directly testing the premise that a general capsid-receptor rule exists.

options.title: In-silico enumeration of capsid–receptor complexes (AlphaFold-class sampling)
options.summary: Sampling capsid variant × receptor ectodomain pairs (AAVR PKD domains, LY6A/LY6C1, CA4, ALPL, LRP6, glycans) with AlphaFold-class modelling, docking and refinement to test whether a compact, transferable binding-signature class exists; the one AAV application used AlphaFold-Multimer plus RosettaRemodel and found its predicted PHP.C2–LY6C1 pose depend on the AlphaFold-Multimer version (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10115422).
options.root_link: Bears on Q1 (measurability) and on whether a compact transferable binding-signature class exists — framer §6.1.
options.compute_open: More parallel compute buys model runs/seeds per (variant × receptor) pair; the largest sampling reported in a cited source is 480 AlphaFold2 predictions per target (32 seeds × 5 models × 3 runs) (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-46715-9); above that it is unknown whether more seeds/MSA subsamples converge on one interface footprint or keep alternating, since the only AAV application found the predicted pose change with the AlphaFold-Multimer version (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10115422).
options.sequential: none: each (variant × receptor) pair and each seed is an independent prediction job only about three recycle iterations deep, so the enumeration splits directly into independent pieces across GPUs.

options.title: Physics-based sampling of capsid–glycan–receptor binding and pH-dependent dissociation
options.summary: All-atom MD and free-energy calculations of capsid–glycan/capsid–receptor binding and endosomal-pH dissociation — the layer where sufficiency of a binding map is decided (framer §6.2); even protein–protein association has been reached only by aggregating adaptive ensemble trajectories (2 ms total) with Markov modelling (https://doi.org/10.1038/nchem.2785).
options.root_link: Bears on Q2 (causal sufficiency) — whether binding energetics plus trafficking kinetics jointly determine transcytosis vs. retention (framer §6.2).
options.compute_open: More parallel compute buys aggregate sampling (ensemble members × trajectory length); the largest amount reported in a cited source is 2 ms of aggregate adaptive MD for a ~100,000-atom protein–protein association (http://ftp.mi.fu-berlin.de/pub/ag-cmb/pyemma-workshop-2018/slides/pyemma-2018-msm-introduction.pdf); above that it is unknown whether more sampling would change any transcytosis-vs-retention ranking of a capsid variant, since no capsid–receptor dissociation free energy at endosomal pH has been published.
options.sequential: One answer waits on time-stepped integration where each step's forces and positions wait on the previous step (2–4 fs per step, so a 1 µs run is 2.5–5×10^8 steps: https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdrun-performance.html), the answer needs tens to hundreds of independent replica runs, and one 50k-atom run keeps one GPU essentially saturated at ~350 ns/day (https://images.nvidia.com/content/tesla/pdf/Molecular-Dynamics-July-2017-MB-slides.pdf). The steps of one trajectory must run in order; the change that runs work at the same time is replacing one long trajectory with many short independent replicas pooled in a Markov state model (or λ-window replica exchange), which pays off only if the rare unbinding/sorting event is likelier from many independent starts than inside one long run; the nearest source that tried it is adaptive ensemble MD with Markov modelling (https://doi.org/10.1038/nchem.2785), with replica-exchange FEP packed onto one GPU via NVIDIA MPS as the nearest throughput measurement (https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/maximizing-openmm-molecular-dynamics-throughput-with-nvidia-multi-process-service).

options.title: Cryo-EM/cryo-ET reconstruction of capsid–receptor footprints
options.summary: Single-particle reconstruction and tomography of capsid–receptor complexes to obtain capsid surface residues, receptor domain and stoichiometry for the binding signature (framer §1.4); AAV2–AAVR structures reach 2.4 Å (https://www.rcsb.org/structure/6NZ0) while tomographic averaging leaves distal AAVR PKD1 densities visible only at ~20 Å (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9278096).
options.root_link: Bears on Q1 (measurability) — whether footprint, receptor domain and stoichiometry can be resolved at molecular resolution (framer §1.4, §3.1).
options.compute_open: More parallel compute buys processed particles/classification jobs and hence resolution; the largest amount reported in a cited source is 30,515 AAV2 particles giving a 1.86 Å capsid map (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-018-06076-6); above that it is unknown whether more particles and finer classification would resolve the flexible AAVR PKD1/PKD3-5 densities that tomographic averaging still shows only at about 20 Å (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9278096).
options.sequential: One answer waits on an ordered processing chain — motion correction → CTF estimation → particle picking → 2D classification → 3D classification → 3D refinement — in which each stage consumes the previous stage's particles and each classification/refinement runs tens of iterations, roughly a dozen ordered stages per dataset with several half-map/classification runs per answer, one GPU kept busy for days per refinement (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9278096). These stages must run in order because each needs the previous stage's output, so wall-time is the sum of the stages rather than their maximum.

options.title: Machine-guided search over capsid sequence space (library design)
options.summary: Training sequence-to-function models on deep mutational scans and searching capsid sequence space to build the matched-affinity/different-footprint panel a decisive answer requires (framer §3.4); ML-guided diversification of one 28-aa AAV2 segment generated 201,426 designed variants yielding 110,689 viable capsids (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-020-00793-4) on top of the complete first-order AAV2 landscape across 735 positions (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7197022).
options.root_link: Bears on the decisive-answer requirement for a ≥50–100 capsid panel spanning matched-affinity/different-footprint and receptor-null variants (framer §3.4).
options.compute_open: settled: wider machine-guided search is a known lever for design yield — 201,426 ML-designed AAV2 variants produced 110,689 viable capsids, 57,348 beyond natural serotype diversity (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41587-020-00793-4).
options.sequential: none: scoring each candidate sequence and each generated variant is an independent per-sequence evaluation, so the search over millions of candidates already splits into independent pieces across GPUs.

options.title: Whole-virion atomistic MD of capsid dynamics and stability
options.summary: All-atom simulation of entire capsids (a few million atoms with solvent; complete virions 10–100 million atoms) to test which binding-altering mutations also destabilise the capsid, the assembly confound in framer §3.5; a whole-virion run has been taken to only 10 ns on a supercomputer (https://i2.riken.jp/download/Q16302.pdf).
options.root_link: Bears on the capsid fitness/assembly confound (framer §3.5) — whether a given binding signature is physically realisable on an intact capsid.
options.compute_open: settled: whole-virion all-atom MD is already known to be compute-bound — an entire few-million-atom virion has reached only 10 ns per supercomputer run (https://i2.riken.jp/download/Q16302.pdf), while the field's stated goal is multi-microsecond sampling of 10–100 million-atom capsids on petascale/exascale machines (https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/dbps/dbp_1.html).
options.sequential: One answer waits on time-stepped integration where each step's forces and positions wait on the previous step — a 10 ns run is 5×10^6 steps at 2 fs (https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdrun-performance.html) and keeps a whole multi-GPU node busy for weeks — and the answer needs a handful of independent runs (the virion study ran several ion-condition/force-field combinations: https://i2.riken.jp/download/Q16302.pdf). The steps must run in order inside a trajectory; only the independent condition runs may proceed at the same time, so the change that helps is running those replicas on separate nodes concurrently, which pays off when each condition equilibrates its observable (ion distribution, stability) independently.
